newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rattled nerves seen plaguing US-led German shares.
newsitem.headline: Rattled nerves seen plaguing US-led German shares.

text.p: Little action was expected on the German share market early on Thursday as investors braced themselves to see what news the afternoon would bring from Wall Street.
"It's just nerves, nerves and more nerves here," said a Frankfurt trader.
"There is no hope of us decoupling from the U.S."

The 30-share IBIS DAX was up 0.19 points at 3,211.13 points at 0712 GMT, after zig-zagging erraticially in the first half hour of trade, then settling eventually above the 3,200-point level, a key technical and psychological support.
June DTB DAX futures were down four points at 3,211 points.
Dow Jones Industrials fell 94 points to 6,517 points on Wednesday, to end up eight percent off their closing high of March 11.
Dealers said that while German shares should not be tracking the U.S. on the basis of economic fundamentals, the psychological impact of Wall Street's decline was immense.
"It's clear we are at a different stage here in the economic cycle -- no-one is talking about a German rate hike today. But it still all depends on Wall Street," a dealer said.
The DAX was seen hovering about the 3,200 point level amid thin trading volumes thought the day.
The Bundesbank's council-making meeting would attract its usual measure of attention but economists were not expecting the central bank to make any move on rates.
Industrial production data for Germany are due at 0800 GMT.

Rising stocks in early trade included chemical group BASF AG which on Thursday predicted it would set fresh records for earnings in 1997, but the bulk of share moves were driven by technical factors, dealers said.
